How do I use it properly the very first time?

Sent · Just now

Rugs USA Bot · AI

Rugs USA Bot · AI says:

Totally get wanting to start off on the right foot with your rug—kind of like breaking in new shoes the smart way.

To use your rug properly the first time:

Unroll and let it relax: Lay it flat so creases and corners can settle; they usually relax in 2–3 weeks. You can:

Back-roll it (roll it the opposite way and leave it for a day or two)
Place heavy objects on corners or bunched spots
As a last resort, gently warm creases with sunlight or a hair dryer held 7–12" away on medium to soften the backing, then flatten.

Set up your rug pad correctly: If the pad sticks out past the rug (totally normal!), trim it:

Lay the pad where you want the rug
Place the rug on top and let them both relax 24–48 hours
Trim the pad vertically and horizontally with fabric scissors so it sits just inside the rug’s edges
Vacuum to smooth out any air bubbles.

Follow basic care from day one:

Vacuum regularly on the lowest setting, without a beater bar if possible, so you don’t pull fibers
Snip any little “sprouts” at surface level instead of pulling them
Clean spills immediately with a clean white cloth, blotting (don’t rub) so stains don’t sink deeper
Rotate the rug occasionally so it wears evenly
Keep it out of continuous direct sunlight to prevent fading

Starting this way sets your rug up for a longer, better-looking life right from day one.
